newsitem.title: USA: NYC weighs selling debt backed by parking fines.
newsitem.headline: NYC weighs selling debt backed by parking fines.

text.p: New York City is analyzing whether to sell its overdue parking fines to a private entity that would use the revenues to back new debt, but no decision is expected before year-end, city souces said Friday.
A spokeswoman for Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said the proposal is still in the early stages. "That is a proposal that has not been reviewed by the mayor, nor approved by the mayor," said Deidre Picou.
The preliminary nature of the plan was also highlighted by a city source, who requested anonymity.
"It's more in the conceptual stage right now, and we're just putting together a package and hopefully are going to present it to a variety of people in the city for further discussions," he said.

While the city has around $1 billion in overdue parking fines, the city source ruled out that any new debt, which would not be issued by New York City, would total as much as that. Saying it was premature to speculate about how much debt might be backed by the revenues, he said, "No, the size of the debt would not be $1 billion."
While the offering would not count under the city's constitutional debt limit, which it expects to hit in about two years, the city source said that was an "unrelated" issue.
Explaining an investment bank was helping the city analyze whether the deal would be favorable, he added, "We might finish the analysis by the end of the year."
